HOW TO USE THE STUDY

From saved inspiration
to a clearer edit.

References become useful when you can name what you see and choose what belongs in your own video.

01 / LOOK

Find a relevant opening.

Start with your footage and message. Compare a face-led opening, a result reveal or a screen demonstration.

02 / UNDERSTAND

Separate the moving parts.

Read the words alongside the frames. Notice what changes, what stays and what the viewer is being promised.

03 / ADAPT

Bring the idea to your edit.

Use the reference to plan your own opening. Test it with your audience and footage rather than copying a whole video.

A NOTE ON THE RESEARCH

Useful observations.
Honest boundaries.

This is an independent study of one creator’s published videos. View counts provide context; they do not prove an editing choice caused a video to perform well. Any discussion of drop-off risk is an editorial estimate, not measured retention data.

Read the scope of the study ↗

BEFORE YOU OPEN YOUR TIMELINE

A few good
questions.

Who is this study for?

Short-form editors and freelancers who want concrete references for talking-head, educational and tutorial Reels. It is a reference study, not a beginner’s editing course.

Does it include presets or project files?

No. The product contains research: frames, timestamps, scripts, classifications, links and five body breakdowns. It does not include footage, plug-ins, presets or editable project files.

Will these hooks make my videos go viral?

There is no performance guarantee. Topic, audience, distribution and the rest of your video also matter. The study gives you examples and observations to inform choices you can test.

How will I purchase and receive it?

Checkout will be available through Gumroad when the study launches. The product listing will explain the delivery format and refund terms before purchase. No payments are accepted on this site yet.
